purpose: The "what teams use it for" band of a product page: a three-column frame whose first cell carries the band's overline, headline, lead and one call to action, followed by one cell per use case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-cases', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `card-grid`, `frame-box`, `overline`, `topic` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.
useWhen: On a product or solution page, right after the opening band, to name the concrete jobs the product is bought for.
Whenever a page needs three to six short, icon-led use cases with one link out to the documentation.
avoidWhen: For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
For use cases that each link to their own page → use `use-case-links`.
Inside another band's cell → compose `topic` directly.
related: topic` — the icon, title and description cell each use case is rendered with.
card-grid` — the frame grid this band lays its cells in.
bestPractices: Keep `items` to four or so; the first cell spans two rows at `lg`, so four cases fill the grid exactly.
Write `title` as the heading the page's outline needs; it is the band's `h2`.
Give `primaryAction` an `href` to the documentation and set `trailing` so the chevron reads as "go".
Leave `eyebrow` as the product name; it is the overline the reader scans first.
